One can think of Moore as asking the proponent of our skeptical argument: which of these do you feel more sure of? Which, if you had to, would you bet your life on?

Moore thinks that we are, and should be, more sure of the second of these. But then why shouldn’t we take his proof of an external world to demonstrate the unsoundness of the argument for skepticism about the external world, rather than the other way around?
